$comment: Single owner of the frontmatter fields recognized by the Claude Code runtime. Read by .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java in `schema` mode. Add a field HERE, never in the Java. Design and rationale: .claude/decisions/0001-schema-frontmatter-extensions.md

injections.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `schema`, applied to every file that mode already visits. A `!`command`` injection runs in the session's persistent shell, at whatever cwd it holds: a `cd` in an earlier Bash call makes a relative `test -f` report a file as absent while it exists, and an injected state that lies fires the entry guard of the skill it belongs to. Requiring the substring below is deliberately blunt — an injection that touches no path at all is also flagged, because `ls -a | head -30` was one of the twelve real occurrences and names no path either. Scope and escapes, each one a false positive the first run produced: only files a `types` match captures are scanned (a decision record or a lessons-learned is prose about injections, and `schema` is handed one on every Edit under .claude/); a fenced code block is dropped; and so is a double-backtick span, which is how markdown has to quote an injection when documenting it. `exempt_patterns` is the escape hatch, one regex per genuinely cwd-independent injection; it is empty on purpose, and an entry added to it needs a reason in the commit. Why this is a hook and not a review item: CLAUDE.md invariant 6. Design: .claude/decisions/0051-frontmatter-injections-cwd-independent.md

arguments.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `schema`, same scope and same two escapes as `injections` above. The runtime interpolates the marker at EVERY occurrence, not only at the interpolation point, so a sentence that talks about the argument arrives with the real value inside it: lessons-learned-012 § 2 caught `/new-feature` telling the model to invoke test-architect `with empty $ARGUMENTS (setup mode)` and the model reading `with empty UC-003-initiate-kyc-verification (setup mode)` — setup mode named by the argument that means design mode. Seven occurrences across six skills, every one of them a sentence about the argument. `requires_field` limits the check to a file that actually receives one; `interpolation_line` is the single allowed shape, a line holding nothing but the marker; `exempt_patterns` is the escape hatch, one regex per line, empty on purpose. Why a hook and not a review item: CLAUDE.md invariant 6 — the defect is invisible in the source and only appears in what the model receives. Design: .claude/decisions/0056-lessons-learned-012-remediation.md

doctor.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `doctor`. `uc_references` sweeps the versioned files for a citation of a `docs/use-cases/UC-NNN-slug/` folder that no longer exists on disk: deleting or renaming a use case folder leaves its citations behind, and each one was correct in the commit that wrote it, so nothing else ever revisits them — lessons-learned-012 § 14 found a `docker-compose.yml` comment pointing at the `25-mensageria.md` of a folder deleted in the run before. Reported, never blocking: a stale citation is a documentation defect and `doctor` is where a person is already reading. Group 1 of `pattern` is the folder path. `root` gates the whole sweep: where that directory does not exist there are no use cases to be stale against, which is the case in this meta-repository — the check belongs to the generated project. `extensions` keeps the sweep off binaries and lockfiles; `exempt_paths` is a prefix match for files that name a folder as illustration rather than reference — a skill body, an agent, a decision record, a lessons-learned.

uc_references.$comment_exempt: Prefixes, matched with startsWith, and written WITHOUT a trailing slash on purpose: a directory prefix spelled with one IS an export residue marker, so this file would report itself as carrying a dead citation on every run. These paths are data, not citations.

settings.$comment: Single owner of what a hook registration may contain. Read by ArchHook.java `schema`, which is also what writes the errors — the runtime itself accepts an unknown event name, a `matcher` on an event that ignores it, and a `type` it has no handler for, all without a word. `match` is a list for the same reason `mcp.match` is: the generated project's hooks live in project-bootstrap's template, and a typo there only surfaces after the project exists. `hook_events` is transcribed from claude-help.md § 8, which ends in "among others" — an incomplete list here would block a legitimate event, so `hook_events_extra` is the escape hatch, one event name per entry, and an entry added to it needs a reason in the commit (same discipline as `injections.exempt_patterns`). `matcher_events` holds the events that actually read a `matcher`; on the rest it is dead configuration that reads as a filter. `entry_types` is repo policy, not a runtime limit: the runtime also serves http/mcp/prompt/agent hooks, and this repo runs commands only. `command_forbidden_chars` enforces exec form — a metacharacter in `command` means a shell string was written where the executable goes, and it silently becomes an argument. Design: .claude/decisions/0053-hooks-in-architect-designer.md

audit.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `audit` mode. The audited set is not listed here: any name that resolves to .claude/skills/<n>/SKILL.md or .claude/agents/<n>.md is recorded, invoked by `/command` or by the model's own Skill/Agent call. Not frontmatter: it lives here because this file is the single owner of every list the hook reads. `redact` runs before the initial prompt is written into the versioned .claude/audit-usage/ report — each `patterns` entry MUST expose the key part as group 1, the replacement keeps $1 and blanks the rest. `exclude_skills` names the skills that carry `disable-model-invocation: true`, and so would be audited, but that OBSERVE instead of producing work — `audit-usage` reads the trail, `arch-doctor` reads the setup. Invoking one closes the run in progress and opens none of its own. Closing was already what happened (any second `/command` closes), so this only drops the empty report an observer would otherwise leave behind; the gain is that a report read mid-session is finished rather than stuck at `⏳ em andamento`. For `audit-usage` it also breaks a feedback loop: reading the trail would append a report about reading, and the next read would be mostly reads. Design: .claude/decisions/0035-auditoria-execucao-hook.md, .claude/decisions/0036-skill-audit-usage.md and .claude/decisions/0038-audit-trail-every-skill-and-agent.md

guard.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `guard` mode, wired only into project-bootstrap/templates/settings.json.example. While a design skill runs (opened by `/<skill>` or a Skill call to one of `design_skills`, closed by the next prompt or by an `executor_agents` Agent call), Write/Edit on `design_forbidden_paths` is blocked unless the call comes from inside an executor agent. Independently, any file under `use_cases_dir`/UC-*/ whose UC-*-spec.md has a status in `frozen_statuses` is blocked, except the executor's single Edit of `status: approved` to `status: implemented`. Why: a design skill once wrote migrations under src/, and a later use case rewrote the specs of an earlier one — both while the skills forbade it in prose.

source.$comment: Where a project pulls this `.claude/` from, and how. Read by `arch-adopt` and by the `export` mode's stamp; validated by `schema`. Deliberately a sibling of `export` and not a field inside it: the exported copy drops the `export` block (its lists describe THIS repository) and keeps this one, which is what lets a project update itself without the plugin. An indirection on purpose — moving from GitHub to a licensing endpoint changes `base_url` and `auth_env`, never the code path that consumes them. `{ref}` is substituted with the resolved ref; `git_url` is what resolves `latest-tag`, through `git ls-remote --tags`, with no API client and no JSON to parse. `auth_env` names an environment variable and never carries its value — invariant 11, the same rule .mcp.json obeys; the header is sent only when the variable is set, so a public repository needs no credential. `--source <local path>` bypasses this block entirely, which is how an unreleased change is tested.

export.$comment: Single owner of WHAT the `export` mode writes into a target project and HOW each piece is transformed. Read by ArchHook.java `export`; cross-checked by `schema` at sweep time, the same way `guard.executor_agents` is. The failure it exists to close is silent in both directions: a skill added to this repo and forgotten here never reaches any project generated afterwards, and an entry left behind after a rename points at a file that no longer exists — neither breaks anything at generation time, only for whoever reads the dead citation inside the project. That is why `include` and `exclude` together must cover every skill and every agent on disk: not listing one is the bug, and `schema` says so by name. Prose counterpart, which branch `feat/bootstrap-invokes-export` replaces with a call to the mode: project-bootstrap/SKILL.md §§ 6.6, 6.7, 6.8, 7. Design: .claude/decisions/0054-deterministic-export-provenance-plugin.md

overwrite.$comment: Not a merge, on purpose: re-serializing the file would reorder its keys and drop its comments, and a real three-way merge is a program nobody asked for. The export refuses a dirty worktree, so the destination's previous content is one `git diff` away and one `git checkout` from coming back. A project that added hook entries of its own loses them here and sees exactly that in the diff.

export.$comment_marker: The cross-check `schema` runs over this block only makes sense in the repository the block describes. `source_marker` is how the mode tells: a directory that exists here and travels nowhere. Without it the check fires in a throwaway tree that merely copied extensions.json — the CI injection sandbox is one — and reports every rule and skill as missing when what is actually missing is the repository.
export.$comment_blueprint: The active blueprint travels with the project, the catalog does not. Without this the yaml that defines a project's architecture can live only in the fetched tree, which is a temporary directory: the stamp records the id, the next update reads that id, the source does not have it, and the export fails at a point where nobody was ever told to keep a file (lessons-learned-011 § 4). Copied for every blueprint, official or not, because at this layer the mode cannot tell one from the other — the fetched tree holds both by then. `{id}` is the blueprint's id.
export.$comment_gitignore: Two lines, opposite decisions, both deliberate. `.claude/audit-usage/` itself is VERSIONED — `history.jsonl`, `nodes.jsonl` and each report belong to the commit of the run that produced them, and `git-publish` stages that directory by default; only the hook's scratch state under `.state/` is ignored. `docs/lessons-learned/` is NOT versioned: those are local notes taken while running the pipeline, not project documentation, and a run that recreates a deleted one writes different text nobody compares. Oscillating between the two is what makes every later diff start dirty — lessons-learned-012 § 15 and § 16.

rules.$comment: Every rule travels; `exclude` is empty on purpose and an entry added to it needs a reason in the commit. `00-index.md` is listed in `body_transforms.rewrite` because its paragraph about architecture_paths cites blueprints/, which the project does not have.

skills.$comment: `keep` is what travels out of each skill directory, and it is a keep-list rather than an exclude-list so that a new subdirectory here (use-case-design/examples/ was the first) stays out by default instead of leaking into every project. `exclude` holds the creation skills: they only serve before the project exists, and inside one they invite the model to regenerate on top of live code.

derived_paths.$comment_exempt: Globs that are valid in any architecture and so need no derivation: they name no package. A rule whose `paths` holds only these is not expected here; one that names a package and is missing from this map would travel with the glob of whichever blueprint happened to be written into the file — gap 8 of lessons-learned-001. `schema` checks both directions.
derived_paths.$comment: A rule with a territory auto-loads by `paths`, and a glob naming a package the active blueprint does not use leaves it silently unloaded. The glob is therefore derived from the blueprint's packages.map — the VALUE, not the key, with `.` becoming `/` — and never copied from the original file. `suffix` selects the packages.map entry whose key ends with it; `key` names candidates in order of preference, first hit wins. A selector that matches nothing and is `optional` copies the rule WITHOUT `paths` (still citable); one that matches nothing and is not optional is a failure of the export, not of the project. No defensive union: this blueprint's glob and no other.

blueprint.$comment: Where the mode reads the architecture from, and how. `vocabulary_anchor_key` names the top-level YAML key the naming-convention comment block sits immediately above — the block is a comment in every blueprint written so far, so it is located by position rather than by a marker, and the position is data because a blueprint that moves it would otherwise need Java changed. Invariant 7: adding an architecture edits no code.

body_transforms.$comment: Applied to every copied text file. A citation to decisions/ has no counterpart inside a project, so it is cut, not rewritten: a sentence that exists only to cite the record goes whole (that is what `sentence_lead_ins` recognizes), and a citation inside a sentence that says something else loses only the citing clause. Whatever survives both is reported by `residue_markers` at the end of the run — a dead path that ships in silence is the failure this whole block exists against, and the report is what makes it not silent.
body_transforms.$comment_replacement: What neither `cut_shapes` nor `sentence_lead_ins` recognizes is a citation inside a sentence that says something else. Deleting the path there leaves the sentence mangled — `- **** —`, `Inherits D15 —.` — and no `residue_markers` entry looking for a path can see what removing the path left behind, so six of them shipped into every exported tree (lessons-learned-012 § 3). The path becomes prose instead: a reader inside a project cannot follow it either way, and the sentence still says what it was written to say. The three shape markers below are the net for the next sentence this does not cover.
body_transforms.citation_replacement: a decision recorded in the meta-repository
body_transforms.$comment_exempt: Two files name these directories on purpose and are not dead paths. `ArchHook.java`'s `export` mode prints them in its own usage and errors, and that mode refuses to run inside a project anyway (no `export` block there). `arch-adopt` talks about the tree it FETCHES, under /tmp, where blueprints/ does exist — cutting those sentences would delete the instructions instead of a citation.

replace.with: the project's packages, documented in the root `CLAUDE.md` and the module `CLAUDE.md` files

replace.$comment: Wrapped across three lines in the source, so the `find` carries the line breaks and the list indentation with it. Brittle by nature — which is what `residue_markers` is for: change the sentence upstream and the export reports the dead path instead of shipping it.
replace.find:
the active blueprint's own
   `packages.map` and its naming-convention comment (`.claude/blueprints/<id>/<id>.yaml`)
   — read the comment, not just the map,
replace.with:
the project's own packages
   and vocabulary, in the root `CLAUDE.md`, the module `CLAUDE.md` files, and
   `.claude/rules/naming.md` § Architecture vocabulary — read the vocabulary, not just
   the package table,

rewrite.anchor: belong to the active blueprint's naming convention
rewrite.replacement:
The names of the use case, its ports, and their implementations change with the
architecture. They belong to this project's own naming convention, fixed at generation
time from blueprint
`{blueprint}`, not to the table above. Where the two disagree, the convention below
wins.

rewrite.$comment: The exported copy keeps no `export` block: its include/exclude lists describe THIS repository's directories, and inside a project `schema` would report the creation skills it excludes as stale entries. Nothing is lost — `arch-adopt` reads the manifest from the copy it fetches, never from the project it is writing into.

rewrite.anchor: `architecture-ddd.md` is the only one without its own `paths`
rewrite.replacement:
`architecture-ddd.md` carries the `paths` fixed at generation time from blueprint
`{blueprint}`. Changing it by hand disables the auto-loading of that rule.

rewrite.anchor: The rules whose territory is a package
rewrite.replacement:
The rules whose territory is a package — `api-rest.md`, `persistence.md`,
`value-objects.md`, `observability.md`, `messaging.md` — had their `paths` written at
generation time from blueprint `{blueprint}`, and they name this project's packages.
A glob edited by hand to a package that does not exist leaves the rule unloaded, in
silence.

mcp.$comment: Validated by ArchHook.java schema, same as `types` above. Design: .claude/decisions/0033-mcp-in-architect-designer.md
